The user wants to buy a musical ticket for "Mamma Mia" on next Friday, and also a train ticket from New York to Chicago on the same day. We need to call two functions: musical_ticket_buy and train_ticket_buy. The user didn't specify the exact date; we need to compute next Friday's date. Today is 2026-10-19 (Thursday). Next Friday would be 2026-10-20. So date: "2026-10-20". For the train ticket: origin: "New York", destination: "Chicago", date: "2026-10-20".

We need to call both functions. According to guidelines, we can only call one function at a time. But we can chain calls? The instructions say "When you do want to call a function, you must do so with a single function call." It doesn't forbid multiple calls sequentially. So we can first call musical_ticket_buy, then train_ticket_buy.

But we might need to ask clarifying question if ambiguous. The user said "下週五" which is next Friday. That is 2026-10-20. Good.

We should proceed to call musical_ticket_buy with show="媽媽咪呀", date="2026-10-20". Then call train_ticket_buy with origin="紐約", destination="芝加哥", date="2026-10-20". However, the function expects English names: origin: string, destination: string. The user used Chinese names. Should we translate? The function likely expects English city names. The user wrote "紐約" and "芝加哥". We could pass those as strings. But maybe better to use "New York" and "Chicago". The user didn't specify but it's safer to use English. The function signature says origin: string, destination: string. No mention of language. But typical usage uses English. Let's use "New York" and "Chicago".

Thus:

First call: musical_ticket_buy({"show":"媽媽咪呀","date":"2026-10-20"}).

Then second call: train_ticket_buy({"origin":"New York","destination":"Chicago","date":"2026-10-20"}).
